gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a laptop which needs a 20 V USB-C source cannot run or charge from a 20 W strip port: under the USB PD power rules a 15–27 W source offers 5 V and 9 V but not 20 V, and Lenovo's manual says a source below 20 V at 2.25 A 'Cannot provide power to the computer or charge the battery'.
standout_why: Compared against rottenwifi.com, inspectandtest.net (best power strip), laptopbee.com and Tom's Guide. Rottenwifi only says that with 15–20 W ports 'a laptop may charge slowly'. Inspectandtest says 'USB-C ports with power delivery can charge many laptops'. Laptopbee says Anker's 20 W port 'negotiates 9V and 12V profiles' and is 'enough for… a MacBook Air under light load'. It also warns that 5 V-only strips can't replace a laptop brick. None of them gives the PD voltage tiers or a laptop maker's 20 V minimum, so none says that a 20 W port (top voltage 9–12 V) can fail to power some laptops at all. The Tom's Guide article body could not be retrieved, so it was not checked.
decides: It confirms a split in the pick. For phones and tablets, a 20 W strip such as the Anker 351 or TESSAN PS07 is fine. For a laptop, only a strip whose USB-C port lists a 20 V profile works, which in this set means the Anker Nano 67 W station or the Prime 140 W. Even then, the laptop has to go in the priority port (USB-C 2 on the A9129), because the other port drops to 20 W when both are in use. ChatGPT's general advice ('laptops typically benefit from 65W or higher') hides the fact that its 'best overall' card, the Anker 351, tops out at 12 V and cannot power a laptop that needs 20 V.

findings.label: Lenovo minimum USB-C source for laptop power (ThinkBook 16p Gen 4 user guide)
findings.value: Source 'should be at least 20 V and 2.25 A'. 'Less than 20 V' at 2.25 A: 'Cannot provide power to the computer or charge the battery'. 20 V at 2.25 A or 3.25 A charges only in sleep, hibernation or powered-off state. Charging while in use needs 20 V at 4.75 A or more.
findings.source_title: Power input through a USB Type-C connector (Lenovo ThinkBook 16p Gen 4 user guide)
findings.note: Lenovo's Table 1, quoted directly. 20 V × 2.25 A = 45 W (my arithmetic). Applies to this Lenovo model and is used here as a named example of a laptop that needs 20 V. Other laptops differ.

findings.label: USB PD normative source voltages by power tier (Power Rules)
findings.value: 15–27 W: 5 V 3 A + 9 V. 27–45 W: 5 V and 9 V at 3 A + 15 V. 20 V appears only in the 45–60 W and 60–100 W tiers. Sink rule: compliant devices must 'guarantee the operation in cases where the Source power (W) ≥ Sink power (W)'.
findings.source_title: Renesas Engineer School: USB Power Delivery: The Technology 1 - Convenience and Safety
findings.note: From Renesas's Table 1, 'Normative Voltages and Currents for source'. In the 15 W-and-under tier Renesas lists 5 V only. The primary USB-IF spec was not opened.

findings.label: USB-C output profiles
findings.value: 5V 3A / 9V 2.22A / 12V 1.67A (20 W max). No 15 V or 20 V profile.
findings.note: Anker spec block. Its highest voltage is 12 V, below Lenovo's 20 V minimum.

findings.label: USB-C sharing rule
findings.value: '20W USB-C charging is only available when the 2 USB-A ports are not in use'
findings.note: Anker's wording. Rottenwifi and inspectandtest already report this sharing rule.

findings.label: Price, anker.com
findings.note: Price on Anker's US product page. The page lists certifications 'TUV / CP65 / FCC / ICES'. It names no UL 1449 listing, and 2,100 J appears only in image alt text.

findings.label: USB-C output profiles
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Charging Station (6-in-1, 67W) A9129 – Anker US
findings.note: This is the only model in ChatGPT's set that lists a 20 V profile. 20 V × 3.35 A = 67 W.

findings.label: Multi-port split and port priority
findings.value: USB-C 1 + USB-C 2: 20 W + 45 W. USB-C + USB-A: 45 W + 12 W. Two USB-A ports share 15 W. 'USB-C 2 (with a computer icon) has higher priority than USB-C 1.'
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Charging Station (6-in-1, 67W) A9129 – Anker US
findings.note: With both C ports in use, the 20 W port falls into the 5/9 V tier, so a laptop must use USB-C 2. The page was 'Sold Out' at anker.com with no price shown. It uses no 'surge' wording, only ActiveShield over-voltage and short-circuit protection.

findings.label: USB output and surge (store listing)
findings.value: USB-C PD up to 20 W (2 ports), USB-A up to 12 W per port, 2,100 J, 8 AC outlets up to 1,250 W. $28.99.
findings.source_title: TESSAN 20W Surge Protector Power Strip PS07
findings.note: Read via storecheck search of tessan.com (Shopify product JSON). Price is the store price today. 20 W puts it in the 15–27 W PD tier (5 V / 9 V), going by Renesas's table.
